newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to sell private bank to settle dues.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to sell private bank to settle dues.

text.p: The Pakistani government on Thursday offered for sale 19.60 million shares of and management of the private Schon Bank Ltd it holds.

The shares on sale, with a face value of 10 rupees each, are owned by the Karachi-based Schon Group, main sponsors of the bank, and had been surrendered to the government in settlement of outstanding dues to the government and financial institutions.

Schon Bank, which rose two rupees at the Karachi Stock Exchange to close at 11.25 rupees, has a paid-up capital of 500 million rupees with total of 50 million outstanding shares, of which 97.42 percent are held by individuals, including sponsors, and 2.58 percent by financial institutions.

"To settle Schon Group's outstanding liabilities... sponsor directors have agreed to sell their fully paid-up shares of Schon Bank and adjust the sale proceeds towards their liabilities," a government Accountability Cell announcement said.

It said expression of interest and offers are invited for the sale by August 12 from parties that should meet the basic criteria and eligibility conditions of the State (central) Bank of Pakistan for ownership and management of a commercial bank.
No Schon Group comment was immediately available.
